content.user_title: Align Projects With a Laravel React Stack
content.value_statement: Teams can drift from established stack choices when building features. This skill guides architecture, tooling, and implementation decisions for a Laravel, React, PostgreSQL, and Pest application.
actual_capabilities: Guides decisions for Laravel, PHP, React, PostgreSQL, Pest, Tailwind CSS, and Redis.
Supports package and library selection against the established technology stack.
Covers Laravel tools including Pint, Herd, Telescope, DebugBar, Wayfinder, and Fortify.
Frames testing work around the Pest framework.
Supports integration choices for Resend, Sentry, and GitHub Actions.
Encourages documentation of technical decisions and dependencies.
limitations: The detailed stack guidance is referenced through an external relative link.
It does not verify installed package versions or project configuration.
It does not provide complete implementation code for each framework.
It is focused on one Laravel and React stack, not broad stack comparison.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Use the skill to choose framework patterns, storage, tests, and services before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review Dependency Choices
use_cases.description: Use the skill to compare proposed packages with the approved stack and existing Laravel tools.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Setup
use_cases.description: Use the skill to align local tooling, testing, CI, caching, and monitoring decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Check Stack Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed feature and explain which parts of the established Laravel, React, PostgreSQL, and Pest stack should guide the implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a feature idea

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for this feature using the approved stack. Include backend, frontend, database, tests, and service integration decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this package choice against the project stack. Explain benefits, risks, alternatives, and whether it fits the existing Laravel and React tooling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Release Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a delivery approach for this change using the project stack. Cover testing with Pest, CI with GitHub Actions, error monitoring, and rollback concerns.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether to add a new test framework for API tests.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Pest first, because the stack already names Pest as the testing framework. It suggests adding feature tests before introducing another tool.

output_examples.input: A team wants to add email delivery to a Laravel feature.
output_examples.output: The skill points to Resend as the named email service and asks the team to document the decision, failure handling, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: A project needs caching for a high-traffic dashboard.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends evaluating Redis because it is part of the stated stack, then pairing the plan with Laravel cache patterns and monitoring.

best_practices: Start with the approved stack before introducing a new package or service.
Document technical decisions when a choice affects architecture or dependencies.
Include testing, CI, and operational concerns in implementation plans.
anti_patterns: Adding duplicate tools when the stack already names a supported option.
Choosing libraries without checking Laravel, React, and PostgreSQL compatibility.
Treating local development, testing, and deployment as separate decisions.

faq.question: What stack does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on Laravel, PHP, React, PostgreSQL, Pest, Tailwind CSS, Redis, and GitHub Actions.

faq.question: Can it choose third-party packages?
faq.answer: It can guide package evaluation against the stated stack and existing project tools.

faq.question: Does it generate complete application code?
faq.answer: No. It guides decisions and plans, but it is not a full implementation template.

faq.question: Does it cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs testing decisions toward Pest, which is named in the skill instructions.

faq.question: Is it useful for deployment planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GitHub Actions, Sentry, Redis, and other operational stack choices.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: They should remove the parent-directory documentation link or bundle the referenced guidance inside the skill.
